- .claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md:52 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: A failed queue read ends the pickup turn instead of proceeding to the janitor.
  WHY: Transient read failures skip session cleanup and stall reporting, and the associated test expects the pickup to continue; reviewers agree on the defect but differ on severity, with Gemini reporting BLOCKER and OpenAI reporting MAJOR.
- .claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md:64 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Stall filing runs only when an entry is new, so a filing that failed previously is not retried on a later wake.
  WHY: The stall is recorded as seen independently of filing success, causing subsequent wakes to skip filing; reviewers disagree on severity, with Gemini reporting BLOCKER and OpenAI reporting MAJOR.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py:142-143, 281-299 | severity=high | confidence=[5]

  PROBLEM: `IMPLEMENT_PLAN_TITLE_PATTERN` does not match issue-mode stage titles that retain a `PR #<pr> — ` prefix after the issue prefix is stripped.
  WHY: Those sessions are classified as `not_ours`, so the janitor does not archive them when their source issues are finished.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py:103-111, 415-419 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: The workflow-template and `.claude` copies of `stale_sessions.py` differ in docstrings.
  WHY: `test_template_parity` asserts byte-for-byte identity between the files and fails when they differ.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py: `next_after_id()` | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The pickup does not persist a continuation cursor when the janitor reaches `--max-pages`.
  WHY: Each wake starts a fresh scan without `after_id`, so eligible sessions beyond the page limit can remain unarchived indefinitely.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml: `Run reviewer models`, lines 4375 and 4401–4412 | severity=high | confidence=[5]

A filing that fails is retried on the next wake, and the janitor runs even when that wake's queue read failed." (README.md, agents.md, commit 060fcef4 summary)
  Expected change site: .claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md step 2, step 3a.4, and step 4
  Evidence of absence: In .claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md, step 2 retains "A failed read (exit 3) → report it and end the turn; the next wake retries" instead of skipping step 3 and proceeding to step 3a; step 3a.4 retains "when any entry was new, run" instead of running filing regardless of whether entries are new; and step 4 lacks the report handling for queue read failures. While test_pickup_files_stalls_on_every_wake_and_runs_the_janitor_after_a_failed_queue_read was added to tests/test_stale_sessions.py to assert these exact strings, .claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md was left unmodified.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- Requirement: "archive an automation session 24 hours after its PR/issue is merged or closed... issue-mode implement-plan stages and checkers once their source issue is finished" (Plan decision D7; README.md; agents.md)
  Expected change site: workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py and .claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py in classify_title()
  Evidence of absence: IMPLEMENT_PLAN_TITLE_PATTERN in stale_sessions.py is anchored to "^implement-plan" without permitting a "PR #<pr> — " prefix, and TITLE_PREFIX_PATTERN only strips "^#\d+ · ". Because numbered titles format stage sessions as "#<issue> · PR #<pr> — implement-plan <slug> — <stage>" or "PR #<pr> — implement-plan <slug> — <stage>", all numbered implement-plan stage sessions are classified as not_ours and excluded from archival.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py: record_stalls (lines 436 and 444)
  PROBLEM: In `record_stalls`, `stall.pop("permission_mode", "")` is called in the first loop for new stalls, and `stall.pop("permission_mode", None)` is called in a second loop for all stalls.
  WHY: The double-pop is redundant and introduces asymmetric fallback defaults. Suggested minimal fix: use `stall.get("permission_mode", "")` during JSON construction in the first loop, then remove the key once in the final cleanup loop.

- .claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md: Step 2’s failed-read branch; `tests/test_stale_sessions.py::test_pickup_files_stalls_on_every_wake_and_runs_the_janitor_after_a_failed_queue_read` | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: A failed queue read still ends the turn instead of continuing to the janitor.
  WHY: A transient queue-read failure skips session cleanup and stall reporting. The test’s assertions for the new branch are also unmet, so this change fails that test.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py: `classify_title()` and `IMPLEMENT_PLAN_TITLE_PATTERN` | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The pattern for `implement-plan` titles is anchored at `implement-plan`, but actual issue-mode stages and checkers are titled `#<issue> · PR #<pr> — implement-plan <slug> — <stage>` (agents.md, lines 839–856).
  WHY: Issue-mode `implement-plan` sessions are classified as `not_ours`; the janitor never checks whether their source issue is finished and never archives them.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py: `next_after_id()`; `.claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md`, step 3a.1–2 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: When the script reaches `--max-pages`, `next_after_id()` returns `None`; the pickup starts each wake with a fresh `list_sessions` request without an `after_id`, and does not persist a continuation cursor.
  WHY: If more than 10 pages fall within the scan horizon, every wake rescans the newest pages. Older eligible sessions beyond that page limit are never reached and remain unarchived.
- .claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md: Step 3a.4; `workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py::record_stalls` | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The pickup runs `permission_prompts.py file --log-dir` only when an entry is `new`; `record_stalls()` marks the `id@updated_at` pair as seen independently of whether filing succeeds.
  WHY: If the issue POST fails on the first wake, the unchanged stall is not new on the next wake, so the pickup skips filing it.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml: Run reviewer models, lines 4375 and 4401–4412 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The supplied check-run context reports that `review / codex-agent` failed on head `060fcef4f9d787f8d9165589184824bd09bc4969` at `Run reviewer models`; `AUTOFIX_FAILURE_FIRST_ERROR` is empty.
  WHY: The workflow propagated a nonzero reviewer result, so this run produced no successful review. The supplied logs do not identify a cause that can be tied to this PR’s changes.
